subject: Environment
sub_topic: Tiger census — All India Tiger Estimation

concepts.name: All India Tiger Estimation (AITE): Methodology Evolution
key_dimensions: Shift from pug-mark census to camera-trap based methodology post-2006 tiger crisis
Role of occupancy surveys, camera traps, and DNA-based fecal analysis in current methodology
Phase-wise structure: Sign surveys → Camera traps → Prey estimation → Habitat assessment
Why pug-mark method was discredited — scientific critique and Sariska scandal trigger

concepts.name: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA): Statutory Basis and Powers
key_dimensions: Established under Wildlife Protection Act 1972, as amended in 2006 — NOT a standalone act
Distinction between NTCA (statutory body) and Project Tiger (centrally sponsored scheme)
NTCA's power to de-notify a Tiger Reserve requires concurrence of State government and CWC
NTCA vs. Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) — overlapping jurisdiction trap

concepts.name: Project Tiger: Launch, Expansion, and Current Status
key_dimensions: Launched in 1973 under PM Indira Gandhi — initially 9 reserves, now 55+ Tiger Reserves
Project Tiger was a centrally sponsored scheme BEFORE NTCA gave it statutory backing in 2006
Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored Scheme with 60:40 Centre-State ratio (90:10 for NE/hill states)
Project Tiger ≠ Tiger Reserves: All Tiger Reserves are under Project Tiger but managed by states

concepts.name: Tiger Reserve: Legal Declaration and Zoning Structure
key_dimensions: Declared by State Government on recommendation of NTCA under Section 38V of WPA 1972
Mandatory two-zone structure: Core/Critical Tiger Habitat (inviolate) + Buffer zone
Core zone must be kept inviolate — no human activity permitted, not even bona fide use
Buffer zone allows co-existence — trap: buffer is NOT a protected area under WPA necessarily

concepts.name: Status of Tigers Report 2022: Key Findings and Records
key_dimensions: India holds ~75% of world's wild tiger population — 3,167 tigers as per 2022 estimate
2022 census: Largest tiger population survey in the world (Guinness World Record)
State-wise rankings: Madhya Pradesh (785) > Karnataka (563) > Uttarakhand (560) — MP reclaimed top spot
Comparison with 2018 data (2,967) showing ~6% increase — rate of growth and concern areas

concepts.name: Camera Trap Technology and M-STrIPES in Tiger Monitoring
key_dimensions: M-STrIPES (Monitoring System for Tigers — Intensive Protection and Ecological Status): mobile-based patrolling tool
Camera trap grid methodology: 25 sq km grid cells, double-camera setup for individual ID via stripe pattern
Individual tiger identification through unique stripe patterns — no two tigers have same stripes
Difference between tiger estimation (periodic census) and tiger monitoring (continuous via M-STrIPES)

concepts.name: Tiger Corridors: Significance, Threats, and Legal Protection
key_dimensions: Tiger corridors connect fragmented habitats — critical for genetic diversity and range expansion
No specific legal protection for corridors under WPA — they fall outside Protected Area network typically
Wildlife Institute of India (WII) maps corridors — 32 functional corridors identified nationally
Key threatened corridors: Terai Arc Landscape, Central Indian landscape, Western Ghats landscape

concepts.name: Wildlife Institute of India (WII): Role in Tiger Census
key_dimensions: WII is the technical partner for AITE — conducts surveys and publishes Status of Tigers report
WII is an autonomous institution under MoEFCC — NOT a statutory body (common trap)
WII vs. NTCA: WII provides science/technical inputs; NTCA provides policy/regulatory framework
WII headquartered in Dehradun — established 1982

concepts.name: Critical Tiger Habitats (CTH): Legal Status and Controversy
key_dimensions: CTH = Core zones of Tiger Reserves, notified under Section 38V of WPA 1972
Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act 2006 vs. CTH — conflict over relocation
Relocation from CTH must be voluntary with rehabilitation package — forced eviction prohibited
Controversy: FRA 2006 rights vs. inviolate status of CTH — Supreme Court interventions

concepts.name: Global Tiger Forum and TX2 Goal: International Context
key_dimensions: TX2 Goal: Doubling tiger numbers by 2022 from 2010 baseline (3,200 target) — set at St. Petersburg Summit 2010
India achieved TX2 goal 4 years ahead of schedule (by 2018 census)
Global Tiger Day: July 29 — declared at St. Petersburg Tiger Summit 2010
Global Tiger Forum: Intergovernmental body for tiger conservation — India is a founding member; HQ New Delhi

concepts.name: Tiger Range States and India's Comparative Position
key_dimensions: 13 Tiger Range Countries: India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, China, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Russia, Thailand, Vietnam
India hosts ~75% of global wild tigers despite having a fraction of original tiger range
Countries where tigers are functionally extinct: Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam — important negative examples
CITES Appendix I listing of tigers — all international trade banned

concepts.name: Sariska and Panna Tiger Reserve: Lessons in Tiger Reintroduction
key_dimensions: Sariska (Rajasthan): First case of complete tiger extinction in a reserve (confirmed 2004-05) — triggered WPA 2006 amendment
Panna (MP): Second reserve to lose all tigers — successful reintroduction program post-2009
Reintroduction protocol: Source population from Ranthambore/Bandhavgarh; NTCA approval mandatory
Sariska scandal exposed failure of pug-mark census — direct cause of methodology shift

concepts.name: Human-Tiger Conflict: Hotspots, Causes, and Mitigation
key_dimensions: Straying tigers vs. conflict tigers — distinction important for response protocol
Compensation mechanism under WPA for livestock/crop loss — state subject with central guidelines
Sundarbans: Unique human-tiger interface — marine context, different from forest-based conflicts
NTCA guidelines: Problem tiger declaration, capture/translocation as last resort before culling

concepts.name: Prey Base and Habitat Quality Assessment in Tiger Census
key_dimensions: Tiger density directly correlated with prey density (ungulates: deer, wild boar, gaur) — line transect method
AITE Phase I: Large-scale occupancy survey of prey and predator signs across tiger landscapes
Habitat assessment uses Remote Sensing (NDVI, forest cover) integrated with field surveys
Minimum viable tiger population concept — small isolated populations face local extinction risk

concepts.name: Frequency and Governance of Tiger Census Cycle
key_dimensions: Census conducted every 4 years: 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022 — quadrennial cycle
2022 census was the 5th cycle — involved 20 states, 600+ protected areas surveyed
States with no tigers but surveyed: Important negative data point for range assessment
Institutional responsibility: MoEFCC (policy) + NTCA (coordination) + WII (technical) + State Forest Depts (field)

concepts.name: Tiger Reserves with Special Significance: Geographic Distribution Traps
key_dimensions: Largest Tiger Reserve: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (Andhra Pradesh/Telangana) — straddles two states
Smallest Tiger Reserve: Bor (Maharashtra) — often confused with Pench
Only Tiger Reserve in Goa: Mhadei — recently notified, controversy with Karnataka over water
Sundarbans Tiger Reserve: Only mangrove tiger habitat in the world; transboundary with Bangladesh

concepts.name: Compensatory Afforestation and Tiger Conservation Finance
key_dimensions: CAMPA funds can be used for buffer zone management but NOT for core zone activities
Tiger Conservation Foundation: State-level bodies to mobilize funds for tiger reserves — mandated by NTCA
Eco-sensitive Zones (ESZ) around Tiger Reserves: MoEFCC notifies, activities regulated but not prohibited
Distinction: ESZ ≠ Buffer Zone — ESZ is outside the Tiger Reserve boundary; Buffer is inside

concepts.name: Poaching, Illegal Trade, and CITES Framework for Tigers
key_dimensions: Tigers listed under CITES Appendix I — strictest protection, commercial trade banned globally
Major demand driver: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) — bones, skin; not food primarily
Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB): Statutory body under WPA, nodal agency for wildlife crime — NOT under NTCA
Operation Thunderbird / Operation Save Kurma: INTERPOL-led operations involving India

concepts.name: Inbreeding, Genetic Diversity, and Meta-population Management
key_dimensions: Island biogeography principle applied to tiger reserves — small isolated reserves prone to local extinction
Meta-population management: Managed gene flow between reserves through translocation
WII's meta-population framework identifies 'source' and 'sink' tiger populations
Genetic bottleneck in tiger populations: Relevant for Sundarbans tigers (island populations)

concepts.name: States Without Tiger Reserves and Recent Notifications: Current Affairs Angle
key_dimensions: States recently getting first Tiger Reserves: Chhattisgarh (Guru Ghasidas), Odisha (Similipal upgraded), Rajasthan expansion
Union Territories with Tiger Reserves: None currently — trap question on Andaman & Nicobar
Northeast India: Significantly underrepresented despite habitat — Dampa (Mizoram), Manas, Orang, Kaziranga, Nameri, Pakke, Namdapha
Proposed Tiger Reserves pending notification: Political and administrative delays — governance angle
